header.running_head: Encouraging People to Proceed in the path of Allaah and Seeing them Off

blocks.text: Encouraging People to Proceed in the path of Allaah and Seeing them Off
Rasulullaah ﷺ Walks with the Mujaahideen and Advises them

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ walked with them up to Baqee Gharqad when he sent them off on an expedition. He then said to them, "Proceed in the name of Allaah. O Allaah! Assist them."[^1]

When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Yazeed (RA) was once invited for a meal, he mentioned to the people that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ bade farewell to an army, he prayed, "In Allaah's care do I hand over your Deen, your trusts and the results of your deeds."[^2]
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Sees the Army of Hadhrat Usaama (RA) off

In a narration discussing the dispatching of Hadhrat Usaama (RA)'s army, Hadhrat Hasan (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left his home to meet the army. As he saw them off, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was walking while Hadhrat Usaama (RA) rode his animal. In the meanwhile, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) was leading Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s animal along. Hadhrat Usaama (RA) said, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! Either you ride or I shall dismount." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) instructed, "By Allaah! Neither should you dismount nor shall I ride! What harm can there be if my feet get dusty for a while in the path of Allaah? A person proceeding in the path of Allaah receives the reward of seven hundred good deeds for every step he takes. In addition to this, his status is elevated by seven hundred degrees and seven hundred of his sins are forgiven." After Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had seen them off, and was returning, he requested, "If you deem it appropriate to assist me with (leaving) Hadhrat Umar (RA) (behind with me in Madinah), please do so." Hadhrat Usaama (RA) then allowed Hadhrat Umar (RA) to stay back.[^3]

Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) dispatched several armies to Shaam, he walked with Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan (RA) who was in command of one of the four armies. Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "Either you ride or I shall dismount." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) instructed, "By Allaah! Neither will you dismount nor shall I ride! I hope to be rewarded for these steps in the path of Allaah."[^4]
